sections.title: Iran answers the blockade with terms and, reportedly, cyber
sections.body: Iran said on 23 November it will use all available means against the US blockade and could reopen Hormuz within two days if hostilities, the blockade and sanctions end. The Wall Street Journal reports US authorities are investigating suspected cyberattacks on up to 50 tankers, with Iran the prime suspect. The US Treasury sanctioned Iranian exchange houses the same day.

sections.title: Attacks on Hormuz tankers reach ten in a week
sections.body: UKMTO reported three tankers struck in the strait and a bulk carrier set on fire off Khor Fakkan on 22 November; gCaptain counts 10 reported tanker strikes since 16 November. Iran blacklisted 26 tugboats and its Guard claims two tankers hit mines on 25 November. The IMO counts 25 seafarers dead, and insurer The Swedish Club advises avoiding the strait.

sections.title: Russia returns to Ukraine's gas and power
sections.body: Russian strikes overnight into 25 November halted a Naftogaz gas production site in Poltava region and cut power in five regions. The Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant lost outside power for the 17th time this year and ran on diesel. Zelensky says 48 Patriot interceptors paid for by allies still await US sign-off.

sections.title: Russian jets press on South Korea
sections.body: About five Russian warplanes entered South Korea's air defence zone on 24 November and approached Ulleung Island without breaching its airspace. Seoul issued its first preliminary air alert over Russian aircraft, scrambled fighters and summoned Russia's attaché. A week earlier Russian aircraft violated Japan's airspace and Tu-95 bombers landed in Vietnam.

sections.title: NATO answers Poland's incursions
sections.body: A Russian drone entered Polish airspace late on 23 November, which Poland's deputy defence minister called deliberate, three days after Russian cruise missiles fell in the south-east; Kyiv Post reports all three were Kh-101s. NATO's council agreed to give Poland an early-warning aircraft and will weigh further air-defence requests next week.

sections.title: North Korea expels Switzerland's envoy
sections.body: North Korea ordered the closure of Switzerland's diplomatic office in Pyongyang on 25 November and told its head to leave within 48 hours, a day after Kim Yo Jong's threat. The trigger was a Swiss sanctions listing of a children's camp accused of taking in deported Ukrainian children. The office had reopened only in October.

key_developments: North Korea ordered Switzerland's Pyongyang office closed and told its head to leave within 48 hours.
Reported tanker strikes near Hormuz reached 10 since 16 November, gCaptain counts; the IMO counts 25 seafarers dead.
Iran blacklisted 26 tugboats serving ships that break its Hormuz rules.
Two Libyan soldiers died after the Benghazi strike; France backed Ukraine's self-defence claim.
Russian strikes halted a Naftogaz gas site; the Zaporizhzhia plant lost outside power again.
US negotiators ruled out troops in post-war Ukraine, the Kyiv Independent reports.
since_last_visit_brief: Reported attacks on tankers near Hormuz reached ten in a week, and North Korea expelled Switzerland's envoy over sanctions tied to deported Ukrainian children.
